blogTitle: Solving Moisture Problems with Safe Bathtub Decor Ideas
videoTitle: Solving Moisture Problems with Safe Bathtub Decor Ideas
script:
Solving Moisture Problems with Safe Bathtub Decor Ideas

Okay — so moisture around the bathtub is honestly one of those problems that sneaks up on you… mould, bad smells, damage to walls — it adds up FAST.

[curious] You know that feeling when your mirror is DRIPPING with condensation every single morning? That's your bathroom telling you the humidity is too high.

A little tip I love: grab a simple hygrometer — anything consistently above 60% humidity is your warning sign to act before mould gets a foothold.

Here's the thing — poor ventilation, hidden leaks, absorbent materials… these all COMBINE to make your moisture problem way worse than it needs to be.

So once you know what you're dealing with, the fun part starts — choosing decor that actually HANDLES moisture instead of fighting against it.

Think non-porous, quick-drying materials — bamboo, teak, ceramic… things that don't hold onto moisture and won't go MANKY on you after a few weeks.

[warmly] And plants — honestly one of my favourites — certain ones like peace lilies or spider plants actually help ABSORB excess humidity while looking beautiful.

Now, keeping a moisture-free bathroom isn't a one-off job — regular checks and CLEANING are honestly what make the biggest difference long term.

Wipe down surfaces after every shower, inspect your decorative accessories regularly… it takes like two minutes and saves you a MASSIVE headache later, trust me.

And swap out any accessories that show signs of mould quickly — keeping things FRESH means your bathroom stays looking as good as the day you styled it.

Ventilation is honestly underrated — running your extractor fan during AND after a shower makes a HUGE difference to how much moisture lingers in the room.

[excited] Right — now the really good bit… making your bathroom feel COSY and inviting, even with all those moisture considerations in mind.

For lighting, think warm-toned bulbs over cool white — they make the whole space feel so much more WELCOMING, and they won't show up every imperfection either.

When it comes to accessories, go for non-porous pieces — think metal hooks, ceramic trays, glass jars — things that WON'T trap moisture and are easy to wipe clean.

Bathroom canvas-wrapped art prints are perfect for damp spaces — they're framed, wipeable, and they give the room such a CLEAN, considered look… one of my favourites.

This set of two small prints is brilliant for tighter wall spaces — you know, that awkward wall next to the tub that you never know what to DO with.

[softly] And if you want something a little softer, these shabby chic floral prints add such a GENTLE, warm feel — beautiful without being fussy.

Safety in wet areas matters just as much as style — non-slip mats are a MUST, and the good news is they come in gorgeous designs now so you don't have to compromise.

This framed set of three is such a smart pick — the frames are sealed, moisture-resistant, and the prints tie the whole room together in a really COHESIVE way.

When selecting any decor accessory for a wet area, look for sealed finishes, waterproof frames, and materials labelled quick-DRYING — those three things are your checklist.

[gently] And this single statement print is a lovely finishing touch — it keeps things SIMPLE, which is honestly the best approach in a bathroom that needs to stay fresh and functional.

The key takeaway? Choose moisture-resistant materials, ventilate properly, add safe accessories… and your bathroom can be BOTH beautiful and completely practical.

Did you know styling your home doesn't have to be guesswork?

From colour theory and design principles to gallery wall layouts and art sizing. Download them all from our site!

Find all you need to transform your home into a calming oasis!

Happy Decorating!
